solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flood defence completed following Depression

blocks.note: f. is the standard abbreviation for following
a low is a weather depression

explanation.surface: A news line about a sea wall finished after a stormy spell.
explanation.walkthrough: Depression looks like the storm the defence was built for, but it is the weather low that ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An overflow is the channel or pipe that carries off excess water so a tank or reservoir does not flood.

clue.text: Old ways in which soldiers brought back commands

blocks.note: rds = roads; ER goes between RD and S
RE = Royal Engineers, turned to ER

explanation.surface: A history of how old regiments received their instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pushes soldiers taking commands back to base; in the wordplay the soldiers are the Royal Engineers, a stock crossword unit, and they are what gets brought back.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: commands and orders are both instructions a superior issues.

clue.text: On a high with my boss coming around in the early hours

blocks.note: the editor is a newspaper setter's boss; E…D
out in the small hours is out late

explanation.surface: Someone buzzing because the boss has dropped round in the middle of the night.
explanation.walkthrough: My boss is ED, the editor, from the setter's point of view as a newspaper contributor.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: being on a high is feeling euphoric, the same state as being thrilled and overjoyed.

clue.text: Jellied eggs somehow go with prawns, fine as a starter

indicators.note: the letters are put together in some other way

blocks.note: first letter of fine, added to the fodder

explanation.surface: A restaurant starter of jellied eggs with prawns, a fine way to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: The menu surface makes jellied eggs sound like a starter; they are the eggs of frogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Frogspawn is the mass of frogs' eggs set in jelly.

clue.text: One often opening doors for an Eton man?

definitions.text: One often opening doors for an Eton man?

blocks.note: read as a doorman or footman, and meant as a connection that opens doors to jobs and clubs
on the surface the person being let in; in the answer the wearer of the school's neckwear

explanation.surface: A servant or doorman holding doors for an Old Etonian.
explanation.walkthrough: The doors are careers, not house doors: the old school tie stands for the network of former pupils who help each other on.
explanation.definitionFit: An old school tie, worn by ex-pupils of a public school like Eton, is shorthand for the favours that network does its members.

clue.text: Good turn-over dessert off the menu?

indicators.note: the pudding is turned over, end to end

explanation.surface: A turnover pastry pudding that the restaurant has run out of.
explanation.walkthrough: A turnover is a real pastry dessert, which hides the instruction to turn PUD over.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish off the menu has been used up, with none left to serve.

clue.text: Coach returning to pick up personnel in plant

blocks.note: a coach is a bus; reversed SUB, as SU…B
HR = human resources, the personnel department

explanation.surface: A coach going back to collect workers at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant reads as a factory for the staff, but it is the definition: a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a bush is one kind of plant, the woody, many-stemmed kind smaller than a tree.

clue.text: Scottish banker wins small house in draw

indicators.note: the river takes, and holds, the pieces that follow

blocks.note: the Dee is a Scottish river, something with banks; DE…E

explanation.surface: A Scottish bank employee wins a little house in a prize draw.
explanation.walkthrough: A banker in crosswords is often a river, which has banks. Draw means depict, not a lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a picture or a line in words is to describe it.

clue.text: Line out of standard vintage songs and burlesques

blocks.note: L = line, removed from OLDIES to leave ODIES

explanation.surface: A cabaret programme of old standards, classic songs and burlesque acts.
explanation.walkthrough: Standard and vintage songs sound like one music-hall list; standard is golf's PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Burlesques are mocking imitations, which is what parodies are.

clue.text: Suit of ice

blocks.note: one of the four suits in a pack of cards
underworld slang for cut gems, from their cold glitter

explanation.surface: A suit made of ice.
explanation.walkthrough: Ice is slang for diamonds, from their cold glitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds are one of the four card suits, and ice is underworld slang for diamonds.

clue.text: Some massager — a serious rubber

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the next words are used

explanation.surface: A masseur who kneads with real force.
explanation.walkthrough: Rubber means one who rubs in the surface, but here it is the thing that rubs out pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: in British English a rubber is the block used to rub out pencil marks.

clue.text: Rash types rush all over the shop with a mum’s car

explanation.surface: Reckless shoppers charging around a store, one of them in mum's car.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator doubles as the surface's picture of people careering round a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Harum-scarums are reckless, impetuous people.

clue.text: Grasses Blunt and Philby etc crossed England

blocks.note: Anthony Blunt and Kim Philby were Soviet spies, communists: RE…DS

explanation.surface: Informers betraying the Cambridge spies Blunt and Philby, who double-crossed England.
explanation.walkthrough: Grasses reads as informers, which fits a clue about spies, but it is the plant. Blunt and Philby were Cambridge-educated Britons who spied for the Soviet Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are tall grasses that grow in wet ground.

clue.text: Loaded, having loads of rooms?

blocks.note: of a gun, with a cartridge put into the chamber
a chamber is a room, so the word read literally means full of them

explanation.surface: Rich, and living in a house with lots of rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Loaded suggests wealth, which suits a big house, but it means a gun with a round chambered.
explanation.definitionFit: A chambered cartridge is loaded in the gun, and something chambered is divided into chambers, rooms.

clue.text: Brave on a mule travelling about Mobile

indicators.note: something travelling about roams from place to place, so the letters wander out of their order

explanation.surface: A plucky rider journeying on a mule around Mobile, Alabama.
explanation.walkthrough: Mobile has a capital M so it looks like the Alabama city, but the capital is only the first word's.
explanation.definitionFit: Something manoeuvrable can be moved about easily: it is mobile.

clue.text: Clergyman missing final church worship

definitions.note: worship is read as a noun here, deep veneration

blocks.note: a reverend, minus its last letter D, leaves REVEREN

explanation.surface: A vicar who skips the last church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Final looks like it goes with church worship, but it takes the last letter off the clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverence is deep respect, and to worship is to revere.

clue.text: Just horrible giving leading female the boot

blocks.note: F = female, the leading letter, removed

explanation.surface: Only a dreadful act, sacking the lead actress.
explanation.walkthrough: Just reads as merely, but it is the adjective: fair and proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Rightful means just, legitimate, as in a rightful heir.

clue.text: Stingy type of heir limiting men with power

blocks.note: a scion is a descendant, an heir: SC…ION

explanation.surface: A mean young heir keeping powerful men on a short leash.
explanation.walkthrough: Stingy looks like mean, a miser; read it as having a sting.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: stingy is read as sting-bearing, and this arachnid carries a venomous sting at the tip of its tail.

clue.text: In Barking, vice-consul gets unsettled

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters are crazed

explanation.surface: A diplomat posted to Barking, in east London, feels restless.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London, which makes In Barking look like a place; barking is also British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter left unsettled is inconclusive, with no decision reached.

clue.text: One spotted in party is old minister

blocks.note: O = old; DO + O, split as DO…O

explanation.surface: Someone seen at a party turns out to be a former government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: One spotted reads as someone noticed, but it is a tile marked with spots.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a tile marked with spots.

clue.text: Minister in a race gets to finish

blocks.note: the TT, the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race

explanation.surface: A politician running in a race manages to cross the line.
explanation.walkthrough: Minister is a verb here: to minister to someone is to look after them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to minister to the sick is to look after and care for them.

clue.text: Music producer hurt over in eastern California

explanation.surface: A record producer injured somewhere in the east of California.
explanation.walkthrough: Eastern California sounds like a region; eastern tells you to read IN from its east end.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica, or mouth organ, is an instrument, something that produces music.

clue.text: Further trouble following Brexit!

blocks.note: the first letter of Brexit, standing for Britain, exits BOTHER

explanation.surface: A grumble that Brexit has only brought more trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Brexit is Britain's exit from the EU, so the clue has B leave the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Further, as in further details, means other, additional.

clue.text: Aussie skippers finally inspect Harrier crash site

explanation.surface: Australian pilots finally inspect the site where a Harrier jump jet came down.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrier looks like the jet and crash like an accident; a harrier is a bird of prey and to crash is slang for going to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is where a bird such as a harrier settles to sleep, or crashes.

clue.text: Fleeing battle (had a fill of killing essentially)

definitions.note: Fleeing is read as a noun, the act of running away

explanation.surface: Running from a battle after having had enough of the slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Had a fill of reads as had enough of; it tells you to fill FIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the noun sense: running away from danger, as in to take flight.

clue.text: Cute icon given makeover failed to impress

indicators.note: the letters are made over into a new form

explanation.surface: A pretty celebrity got a makeover that nobody liked.
explanation.walkthrough: The makeover is literal: the same eight letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: an argument that makes no impression on someone is said to have had no effect on them at all.

clue.text: Vessels left by those eating no starter

indicators.note: the diners lose their first letter

blocks.note: diners, minus the D, leave INERS

explanation.surface: Plates left behind by diners who skipped the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Vessels and starter suggest dishes at a meal; the vessels are ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Liners are large passenger ships, vessels.

clue.text: A drug rock

blocks.note: a class of drug, anabolic kinds used by bodybuilders

explanation.surface: Drug slang: rock is a street name for crack cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock is a slang word for crack cocaine, so A drug rock reads as one phrase; the rock is in space.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a rocky body orbiting the sun.
